value: BOUNDARY ON claim.law.ternary-diamond-reaches-forward-branch-pair-at-cost-of-temp-result-register.20260831.v1. That law is correct that the forward unfused pair (`bCOND <next insn>` followed by `b <merge or epilogue>`) is reachable by an arm-swapped ternary with the EMPTY arm first, and it is naturally read as a general spelling for that branch shape. IT IS NOT GENERAL: THE TERNARY ONLY SPLITS THE PAIR WHEN ITS RESULT IS CONSUMED. In the parent law's verified case the ternary was ASSIGNED to a live local (`node = (idx < 0) ? node : ...`), so the front end had to materialise a result register and a merge block, and it is that materialisation - not the ternary syntax - that forces the empty arm to become its own basic block carrying the lone `b`. When the ternary appears as a bare expression STATEMENT whose value is discarded, as it must in a void function, MWCC folds the empty arm away and re-emits the ordinary single inverted conditional, giving byte-for-byte the same object as the plain `if`. MEASURED: on DoPolyInst, a void function, the arm-swapped ternary and an if/else statement form produced IDENTICAL objects (real 15, insns 32/31, multiset 3t, same diff cluster) - two identical A/Bs. A SECOND OBSERVATION FROM THE SAME PROBE, useful well beyond this function: the nested ternaries reproduced the function's inner if/else chain BYTE-FOR-BYTE, including its fused inner guards, so ternary and if/else are NOT distinct lowering paths in MWCC's front end whenever the value is unconsumed - do not reach for a ternary to change branch layout in a void context at all. THE CHEAP IN-FUNCTION CONTROL, which should be read BEFORE spending any probe on this class: check whether the function already contains a void early-return guard. DoPolyInst's own first guard `if (inst->_02 != 0) return;` compiles FUSED to a single `bne ->epilogue`; a function that fuses its own void guards will fuse the one you are trying to split, and the pair you are chasing must therefore come from a construct that yields a value. CONSISTENT WITH, AND SHARPENING, claim.law.empty-block-branch-pair-splits-forward-vs-backedge: both of that law's positive controls for the reproducible forward spelling (OSRtc.c::ReadSram `if (!EXILock(...)) { return 0; }` and atree.c::AtreeFindNodeIdx `if (strncmp(...) == 0) { return i; }`) are guards in VALUE-RETURNING functions whose block carries a return value, even where that value is already in r3 and the block is empty of instructions. Read the two laws together as one rule: the forward unfused pair is reachable only where a VALUE must be delivered at the merge, whether by a ternary result or by a returned value; in a void statement context it is unreachable from portable C and the residual should be parked on branch form or handed to a WebFrank branch-form rule.
